stem: A 9-year-old with known diabetes develops nausea and repeated vomiting during an intercurrent illness; how should these symptoms be interpreted on sick-day management?

options.text: As signs of insulin deficiency and ketosis until proven otherwise
As reassurance that ketosis is unlikely
As evidence that insulin should be withheld until oral intake improves
As proof of isolated gastroenteritis with no diabetes relevance
As a reason to delay any diabetes review until the next day

explanation: Signs of insulin deficiency and ketosis until proven otherwise is the correct interpretation. In a child with diabetes who is unwell, nausea and vomiting should be treated as warning features that may indicate ketosis and need prompt attention.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Diabetes Sick Day Management

optionExplanations.A: Correct because nausea and vomiting on a sick day are treated as signs of insulin deficiency and ketosis until proven otherwise.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because these symptoms are not reassuring in a child with diabetes; they raise concern for ketosis.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because insulin should not be withheld on this basis; the concern is that insulin deficiency may be present.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because vomiting in a child with diabetes has important diabetes implications and should not be dismissed as unrelated gastroenteritis.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because sick-day symptoms warrant timely assessment and management rather than waiting until the next day.
